text:
Broad Street Hockey summed up Sean Couturier's season in a headline: his role has changed, but the Flyers still need him. At 33, a Selke winner six years ago, he plays 16 minutes a night and has 5 points in 18 games.

The offense isn't really the job anymore. Evolving-Hockey had him in the 96th percentile last season for taking chances away, and his value came mostly from even-strength defense. The problem this year is that the Flyers take only 40% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) at five on five with him on the ice. They're about two points worse without him, so it's mostly a team problem, but a defensive center can't fix it alone.

He's shooting 5.3% against a normal range of 10% to 14%, so a few more goals should arrive. His skating numbers (5th percentile top speed) are what you'd expect from a veteran who wins with positioning. PHLY Sports' Charlie O'Connor noticed a new line on Nov. 5, Couturier with Owen Tippett and Barkey. We project about 33 points. For Philadelphia, the hope is that his line keeps the other team's best quiet while Michkov and Zegras find goals.
headline: Couturier's role changed
